solutions.check: 28 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Strangely non-American POTUS, Net star of religion

indicators.note: something done strangely is done in an odd order, so the letters are rearranged
non-American asks for the US abbreviation to be taken away from the word beside it

parts.note: President of the United States, taken as written before US is removed
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sports star rises oddly to become President, without being American.
explanation.walkthrough: POTUS loses US to leave POT; POT, NET and STAR are then rearranged into PROTESTANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A Protestant church or believer belongs to the Reformed branch of Christian faith, so the word describes a religious affiliation.

clue.text: Own up about "heartless Piccadilly", being an agent?

indicators.note: about means going round, so the confession word wraps around the other letters

parts.note: to sing is slang for confessing to the police

indicators.note: removing the heart leaves only the outside letters of the place name

parts.note: the first and last letters of the London street

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to confess to an incident in central London, as if they were a secret agent.
explanation.walkthrough: Piccadilly is a famous street in central London; to sing is underworld slang for confessing to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Spying is the activity of a secret operative gathering intelligence, which is what working as an agent means here.

clue.text: A bastard overturned schedule — troublemaker

parts.note: taken as written
git is British slang for a contemptible person

indicators.note: overturned means turned upside down, so in a down clue the word for schedule is read backwards

parts.note: a rota is a roster or timetable of duties

explanation.surface: Some unpleasant person has upended the work timetable, causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: A + GIT + ROTA reversed (ATOR) gives AGITATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An agitator stirs up public unrest or protest, making them someone who deliberately causes disturbance.

clue.text: Trump, dismissing politician: "hunt out fake news!"

indicators.note: out here means put out of place or disordered, so the letters are rearranged
dismissing sends something away, so the politician's letters are removed from the name

parts.note: the President's surname, taken as written
MP is a Member of Parliament
taken as written

explanation.surface: Trump, firing an official, rails against fake news and urges a hunt for it.
explanation.walkthrough: TRUMP without MP leaves TRU; TRU and HUNT are mixed up to give UNTRUTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Fake news is false information presented as fact, which is a lie or falsehood.

clue.text: Stuff bra out, stuck into French chip

indicators.note: stuck into means pushed inside, so the jumbled letters are placed within others
out means disordered here, so the underwear letters are mixed up

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for French
taken as written, then rearranged
IC is an integrated circuit, a silicon chip

explanation.surface: Underwear is thrown out and lands on a French fry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' looks like a verb but is a noun here, and the chip is electronic rather than a French fry.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff in the sense of material or cloth is a synonym for textile or woven material.

clue.text: Boris ultimately left in clutches of assailant — mule!

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the name is kept

parts.note: the final letter of Boris

indicators.note: being in someone's clutches means being held by them, so one letter sits inside another word

parts.note: a mugger is someone who attacks to rob
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Boris ends up in the grip of an attacker who turns out to be a mule.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the left-hand abbreviation goes inside the attacker; the letter from Boris sits in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mule is slang for someone who carries drugs across a border, an illegal courier of contraband goods.

clue.text: Broadcast 'right look' for Kim Jong-un's idea of news?

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken over the airwaves, so the phrase is judged by its sound

parts.note: proper means right and a gander is a look

explanation.surface: A dictator's news broadcasts are only the right way of seeing things.
explanation.walkthrough: To have a gander is British slang for taking a look; PROPER GANDER said aloud is PROPAGANDA.
explanation.definitionFit: North Korean state media issues only regime-approved messaging, so its so-called news is political indoctrination material.

clue.text: Not very clever, getting upset over Labour leader's slight

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the word for not very clever is turned round
over here means covering all around, so the reversed word encloses the single letter

parts.note: dim means unintelligent

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so only the opening letter of Labour is used

parts.note: the first letter of Labour

explanation.surface: A dim figure takes offence at a slight from the Labour leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slight' looks like a noun meaning an insult, but it is the adjective meaning faint.
explanation.definitionFit: Slight and mild both describe something gentle, faint or of little intensity.

clue.text: see 24dn.
(& 25ac.) Dope on sources of the Economic Reform Bill, put to great use by Trump

definitions.text: put to great use by Trump

parts.note: a twit is a fool, as is a dope

indicators.note: sources are where things start, so only the opening letters of the following words are taken

parts.note: first letters of these three words
a bill is an account of money owed

explanation.surface: A fool backs a reform bill on the economy that Trump makes much of.
explanation.walkthrough: TWIT + TER + ACCOUNT gives TWITTER ACCOUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Trump's social media profile on that platform was famously his main channel for posting announcements and attacks.

clue.text: Proper clever, ignoring Boris's lead

indicators.note: ignoring leaves something out, so that letter is dropped from the word for clever

parts.note: bright means intelligent

indicators.note: a lead is what goes in front, so the opening letter of Boris is meant

parts.note: first letter of Boris

explanation.surface: Someone properly clever pays no attention to Boris's lead.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIGHT without its B leaves RIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper and right are synonyms meaning correct, fitting or as it should be.

clue.text: Pissed after change of leader — frightful mess

indicators.note: a change of leader swaps out the first letter for a different one

parts.note: tight is British slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Someone drunk after a leadership change makes a frightful mess.
explanation.walkthrough: Pissed is British slang for drunk, not angry. TIGHT gets a new first letter, S, to make SIGHT; the crossing letters confirm which.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking a sight is an idiom for appearing a ridiculous, unkempt spectacle, a dreadful state of disarray.

clue.text: Rude — time to cut down on Streep-like stuff

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
Meryl Streep is a film actor, so what she does is act
to cut down on something is to do it less

explanation.surface: A crude Hollywood star is told it is time to tone down the acting.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says it is time to ACT LESS: T + ACT + LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactless means lacking diplomacy or sensitivity, so a tactless remark is impolite and offensive.

clue.text: "Welcoming transformed USA with a lot less love" — politician

indicators.note: something transformed has changed its form, so these letters are rearranged
less means minus, so the letter for love is subtracted

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
a Tory is a Conservative politician in Britain

explanation.surface: A Tory politician hails a changed America with much less affection.
explanation.walkthrough: USA and A LOT, without O, are rearranged to SALUTA, then TORY is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Salutatory is a formal adjective describing a greeting or opening address, so it means expressing a salute.

clue.text: State gets Mark ace Eye application

parts.note: MA is the postal abbreviation for Massachusetts
a scar is a mark on the skin
A is the card abbreviation for ace

explanation.surface: Mark, a top performer for Private Eye, gets attention from the state.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark and Eye are capitalised to look like a name and a magazine; they are a scar and the organ of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascara is cosmetic colouring brushed onto the lashes, so it is something applied to the eyes.

clue.text: Takes Tebbit's advice, seizing commercial holiday islands

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold of, so the bike word holds the advertising letters inside

parts.note: Norman Tebbit, a Thatcher-era minister, said his jobless father got on his bike to look for work
a commercial is an advertisement, an ad

explanation.surface: Someone follows a Tory grandee's advice while grabbing an advert for a beach holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Tebbit's 1981 'get on your bike' speech is a famous British political phrase, so his advice is to ride a bike.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cyclades are a group of Greek islands in the Aegean, popular resort destinations such as Mykonos and Santorini.

clue.text: Snort cocaine right inside sleazy hotel

parts.note: C is slang shorthand for cocaine

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so one letter goes into the rearranged word
something sleazy is disreputable and out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone sniffs coke in a seedy hotel room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snort' suggests drugs in the surface, but it is the definition, meaning a laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: A chortle is a gleeful chuckle, and a snort can be a burst of laughter through the nose.

clue.text: "One force in the House — topping!"

indicators.note: in places the first pair of pieces inside the word for house

parts.note: a house is a home
the Roman numeral for one
the Criminal Investigation Department, the British police detective branch

explanation.surface: A cheer for a lone police officer in the House of Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: Topping is British slang for killing, especially by execution; the exclamation mark makes it look like praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Topping someone in British slang means killing them, so a topping is an unlawful killing or murder.

clue.text: Uranium poo container takes hospital down

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium

indicators.note: takes means admits or holds, so the hospital letter is placed within the container word

parts.note: a nappy is the British word for a diaper
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A radioactive nappy gets carted off down to the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' looks like a direction to the hospital but is the definition, meaning sad.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling down is an idiom for being sad or dejected, which is to be miserable.

clue.text: Northern town has goods on Blair? Almost

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: stock is goods held for sale
Tony Blair, the former Labour Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A northern town has dirt on Tony Blair, nearly.
explanation.walkthrough: STOCK + TONY without its last letter gives STOCKTON.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockton-on-Tees is a market town in north-east England, in County Durham historically.

clue.text: see 26ac.
Blemish on Theresa's no. 1, as heard in church?

parts.note: a mote is a speck or particle

indicators.note: number one means the first, so only the initial letter of Theresa is used

parts.note: first letter of Theresa

explanation.walkthrough: MOTE + T. 'As heard' suggests a sound-alike, but it belongs to the definition: a piece one hears sung in church.
explanation.definitionFit: A motet is a short sacred choral composition, the sort of music a congregation listens to in a service.

clue.text: There's no denying that much of Donald is malice primarily

definitions.note: a phrase standing for a noun: a statement nobody denies

parts.note: Donald Trump
taken as written

parts.note: first letter of malice

clue.text: Would-be elder statesman's second-rate retreat

parts.note: B grade means second-rate

clue.text: (& 9dn.) Unsavoury bunch of banker types starts importing dodgy load

starts are beginnings, so the first letters of banker and types are taken

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: The two-word answer spans both linked lights, with 'of banker types' running on from the definition into the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad lot is an idiom for a disreputable person or group, people of dishonest or unpleasant character.

clue.text: see 10ac.

taken as written

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
